name: Nam Et-Phou Louey National Protected Area
blurb: Hill forest where sambar, dholes and clouded leopards hunt in tiger country.

tip.title: Thin out the sambar
tip.text: Sambar are the main named prey here. Set Sambar to -100% and watch the dhole, clouded leopard and tiger, and the water monitor that scavenges their kills.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Nam Et-Phou Louey National Park

notes: The species list comes from GBIF occurrence records inside a circle around the park, so it can include nearby areas. Feeding links come from GloBI records and the sources listed where they state them; others are general ecology and are illustrative.

nodes.desc: Drives growth in the forest canopy and the grassy clearings and scrub left by past disturbance.
Annual rainfall is about 1,400 to 1,800 mm, falling mostly from May to October. The area also feeds many rivers, including Mekong tributaries.
Holds the nutrients that the evergreen and semi-evergreen forest draws on, and is refilled by decomposers.
Forest figs bear fruit that many monkeys, apes and birds feed on.
A big deer that eats grasses, foliage, fruit and shrubs. It gathers at the Poung Nyied salt lick and is the main named prey of the reserve.
A small forest deer, also called barking deer, that eats leaves, fruit and shoots.
A forest monkey recorded in the reserve that eats fruit, seeds and leaves.
An omnivore that eats fruit, nuts and acorns, insects and larvae, and carrion.

nodes.name: Red-whiskered bulbul
nodes.desc: The best-recorded bird in the surrounding area. It eats fruit and insects, and spreads seeds.
A small forest cat that eats small mammals and birds. Recorded in camera traps in the area.

nodes.name: Asian water monitor
nodes.desc: A large lizard that hunts a wide range of prey and often eats carrion, helping clean up dead animals.
Once the top predator here, with sambar as a main prey. There have been no park records since 2013, so it is now considered lost from Laos.
A pack-hunting wild dog that mainly takes medium and large deer and boar. It has been studied in this reserve and is hit hard by snaring.

nodes.name: Fungi, termites & bacteria
nodes.desc: Break down fallen leaves, wood and dead animals and return nutrients to the soil.
